title: Eurostat euro-area HICP, complete August 2026 data (12:00 CET / 06:00 ET) — the component detail behind the 3.3% flash
source: EST: ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-01092026-ap — the August 2026 flash estimate (published 2026-09-01), re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 for this event's initial research, which names the follow-up verbatim: 'The next release with full data for August 2026 is scheduled for 17 September 2026.' Independently corroborated by a SECOND primary that also supplies the clock the Eurostat page omits: the ECB statistical release calendar (ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/statscal/ges/html/sthicp.en.html, fetched direct 2026-09-08), whose row reads '17/09/2026 12:00 CET - Euro area seasonally adjusted HICP (Dataset: HICP) Reference period: Aug-2026', with the next cycle at 02/10/2026 15:00 CET (September flash) and 16/10/2026 12:00 CET (September complete). 12:00 CET is 06:00 ET, i.e. before the US open. Realized cadence corroborates on five consecutive months of complete releases landing on the 16th-20th of the following month: 2-16042026-ap (16 Apr, March data), 2-20052026-ap (20 May, April), 2-17062026-ap (17 Jun, May), 2-17072026-ap (17 Jul, June), 2-19082026-ap (19 Aug, July). Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because this calendar carries no confirmed source prefix for a non-US statistical agency — the same taxonomy reason ecb-decision-2026-09-10 is filed estimate despite a direct ECB primary. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research, over the single proposal proposals/eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17.from-cpi-2026-09-11.json (read first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md; it is now shadowed and stays where it is). The proposal's finding stands and one of its citations is corrected: it described 2-19082026-ap as 'the sibling flash release for July', but that document is the July COMPLETE release (the July flash was 2-31072026-ap, 31 Jul). The correction strengthens the entry rather than weakening it — 2-19082026-ap is direct evidence of the flash-then-complete cadence AND of an unrevised headline. THE HEADLINE IS ALREADY PUBLIC AND HAS NOT MOVED AT A COMPLETE RELEASE IN FOUR CONSECUTIVE MONTHS: April 3.0 -> 3.0, May 3.2 -> 3.2, June 2.8 -> 2.8, July 2.9 -> 2.9 (flash vs complete, both figures read off the primaries). Eurostat's own HICP information-on-data page goes further and says a flash-vs-final difference is not treated as a revision at all. So 09-17 is not where the August number becomes known — it became known on 09-01 (3.3%, from 2.9%; energy 14.3% vs 10.3%, services 3.0% vs 3.3%, non-energy industrial goods 1.2% vs 0.9%, food/alcohol/tobacco 1.2% stable, core ex-energy-and-food 2.4% vs a 2.5% consensus, m/m +0.4%). SEQUENCING IS THE VERDICT: 09-17 lands AFTER ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and AFTER fomc-2026-09-16, so it cannot inform either meeting; the ECB had this data as the flash nine days before it decided. What the complete release genuinely adds is the contribution table, the national breakdown (July: Sweden 0.3% low, Romania 8.2% high — a 7.9pp spread) and item detail. Impact LOW and symbols [] deliberately: no house playbook is rates-keyed, no tracked name carries euro-rates or euro-inflation exposure, and a 06:00 ET statistical confirmation of a number published sixteen days earlier has no price channel to this book. What the entry buys is coverage — this calendar tracks eight ECB entries and, before this one, zero Eurostat inflation releases, which is why the August flash took a week to reach the US CPI ledger. Read-across limit, stated so it is not overread later: euro HICP is NOT US core CPI — it carries no owners'-equivalent-rent, where US core's heaviest weight sits, and its energy weight (~9.1%, implied from the July complete's own rate-and-contribution pair) is higher, so any comparison is directional and never quantitative. A further trap for the item detail: the HICP was rebased and reclassified in February 2026 (ECOICOP 2 / UN COICOP 2018, games of chance folded into recreation services, reference period 2025=100), so 09-17's sub-indices are not apples-to-apples against 2025 vintages. Proposed and filed as an estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
